text.arabic_uthmani: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يُنَادَوْنَ لَمَقْتُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ مِن مَّقْتِكُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ إِذْ تُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلْإِيمَٰنِ فَتَكْفُرُونَ

words.gloss_range: emphatic clause-opening assertion that governs the condemned class and sets the announced verdict as settled rather than debatable
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) opens with emphatic certainty before the passive proclamation is heard. It governs the class and lets the later call disclose a verdict already installed as settled. The force also works in layers: the outer assertion prepares the inner emphatic comparison, so the ayah moves from the previous mercy-prayer setting into public rebuke rather than from neutral report into explanation.

topics.headline: settled assertion governs the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the condemned class and verdict as settled before the public proclamation unfolds.
topics.reason: Local grammar marks an emphatic annulling particle governing the relative subject and predicate, while the CRITICAL rows press its full-clause reach.

topics.headline: outer assertion prepares inner rebuke
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a layered scene: assertion hands the condemned group into a quoted judgment after the previous mercy-prayer setting.
topics.reason: The quoted complement and boundary rows support an outer assertion frame that turns into direct public verdict.

words.gloss_range: definite relative head that classifies a group by completed denial and keeps later pronouns tied to the same referent
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) does not merely point to people already known; it builds the group through the following completed denial. That classifying function keeps the offense before the summons and also preserves referent continuity when the same group is later addressed as you. The word is therefore a hinge between third-person classification and second-person accusation.

topics.headline: relative head makes denial class-defining
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the group is syntactically constituted by denial before the proclamation reaches them.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is specified by the following relative-clause verb, so the offense is structurally prior to the summons.

topics.headline: same group becomes direct addressee
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks one referent from third-person description into second-person confrontation instead of hearing a new group appear.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence ties later suffixes and second-person verbs back to the same relative head.

words.gloss_range: completed Form I denial defining the group; locally a culpable refusal of faith, not neutral nonbelief or a derived causative posture
words.root_gloss_range: root field of covering, refusal, ingratitude, and denial; this ayah selects culpable refusal of the offered faith relation while retaining the covering image as moral pressure
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) classifies the group by a completed Form I act of denial. In this ayah the root's covering-refusal field is narrowed by the later call to faith: it is culpable refusal of an offered trust relation, not mere absence of belief. The same root returns at the end in direct address, so the opening label becomes the closing indictment. The opening phrase shape also recalls a closed-refusal formula (2:6), now voiced as afterlife accusation.

topics.headline: completed denial defines the group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees denial as the completed basis of the class before judgment is announced.
topics.reason: The perfect verb completes the relative clause and supplies the classifying action for the relative head.

topics.headline: covering image narrowed to faith-refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears denial as a covering of owed recognition after a faith-call, while local context prevents a generic dictionary expansion.
topics.reason: The later invitation to faith selects refusal of trust as the local sense while preserving the root image of covering owed recognition.

topics.headline: Form I keeps blame direct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that blame rests on their own basic act of denial, not on a causative or reflexive derived posture.
topics.reason: The aligned form is Form I perfect, which supports direct agency and blocks importing derived-form force.

topics.headline: opening denial returns at closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a denial frame: the ayah begins with completed denial and ends with the same root as direct accusation, with the broader closed-refusal formula recalled (2:6).
topics.reason: The same root occurs at the opening and closure, and the concrete formula link to 2:6 supports retaining the echo as a specialized afterlife indictment.

words.gloss_range: passive public proclamation over the condemned group; a raised verdict-call contrasted with the earlier invitation-call
words.root_gloss_range: root field of raised calling, public summons, and projected address; local Form III passive selects exposed proclamation rather than private invitation
words.prose: {{ar:يُنَادَوْنَ}} ({{tr:yunādawna}}) is the asserted predicate: they are made the patients of a public proclamation. Its passive Form III call suppresses the herald and foregrounds exposure, while its register differs from the later invitation-call; public calling scenes such as 7:44 keep that exposed register visible. The ayah therefore stages two calls: the later verdict-call makes audible the earlier refused opportunity, and the recurring nasal-dental call texture gives the reversal a heard trace.

topics.headline: passive proclamation exposes the recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the scene spotlights being made to hear a public verdict, not identifying the announcer.
topics.reason: The passive predicate completes the assertion frame, and the Form III/root evidence supports public directed proclamation.

topics.headline: verdict-call contrasts with invitation-call
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes the exposed verdict-call from the earlier responsive invitation-call, including a public calling scene parallel (7:44).
topics.reason: The ayah contains two passive call verbs with different roots and discourse roles, and the concrete link to 7:44 supports the public-address register.

topics.headline: call opens quoted rebuke
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the proclamation as the hinge into quoted speech, with sound texture supporting the call-to-call reversal.
topics.reason: Attachment marks the following verdict as the quoted complement, while the sound row adds a local cadence payoff.

words.gloss_range: inner emphatic prefix attached to the maqt clause, reinforcing the comparative verdict without adding lexical content or prepositional governance
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) is the inner intensifier attached to the comparison's first noun. It is not a preposition or oath particle here; it reinforces the proposition that divine maqt is greater. Because it follows the outer emphatic opening, the verdict is pressed twice: first by assertion, then by the hardened comparative claim.

topics.headline: emphasis scopes over the comparison
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the comparison introduced as reinforced truth, not as a neutral ranking or a new governed phrase.
topics.reason: The particle is prefixed to the nominal subject of the comparative clause and functions as emphasis without adding lexical argument structure.

topics.headline: inner intensifier follows outer assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the two-layer confirmation: the ayah asserts the group, then hardens the verdict inside the quoted speech.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows link the opening emphatic particle and inner lām as a rhetoric of resistant-hearer confirmation.

words.gloss_range: specific divine maqt in construct with the divine name, a severe condemning rejection made measurable as the subject of the comparison
words.root_gloss_range: rare root field of severe aversion, abhorrence, and condemning rejection; the ayah concentrates it by repeating the root in divine and human measures
words.prose: {{ar:مَقْتُ}} ({{tr:maqtu}}) names the first maqt as a definite construct tied to the divine name and made the subject of the ranking. The verbal noun lets severe condemning rejection stand as something measurable, while the repeated rare root makes the whole comparison turn on maqt rather than on vague emotion. The passive-detested image in the root family prepares the later self-object without replacing the local noun sense. Intertextual pressure from maqt with greatness language (61:3; 40:35) keeps the field forensic: contradiction is being condemned. Against the prior mercy-success outcome, this word turns the register toward divine rejection.

topics.headline: specific divine maqt becomes the ranked subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first maqt is a specific divine evaluation placed as the entity being ranked.
topics.reason: The construct with the divine name makes the verbal noun definite, and predication evidence makes it the subject of the elative.

topics.headline: rare maqt field carries severe rejection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels maqt as severe condemning aversion, while the passive-detested image prepares the later self-object rather than replacing the local noun sense.
topics.reason: The dictionary and distribution rows support severe rejection and rare concentration; the passive derivative is kept as image pressure tied to the later object.

topics.headline: maqt repetition organizes the comparison
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine maqt and self-maqt as one measuring field in which human self-revulsion cannot set the scale.
topics.reason: The repeated root creates a structural pair around the elative comparison and the later explanatory memory.

topics.headline: forensic maqt answers contradiction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this maqt to contradiction-condemnation language (61:3) and same-surah maqt-with-greatness recurrence (40:35), while the boundary turns prior success language into forensic rejection.
topics.reason: The concrete references and boundary rows support retaining the inter-ayah and local-surah payoff without making them control the grammar.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name in genitive construct, anchoring the first maqt to the decisive evaluator rather than to a generic divine category
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine-name field with disputed derivational background; locally the proper name functions as the definite genitive source of the verdict
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) completes the construct and names the source of the first maqt before the elative announces its superiority. The proper name makes the evaluation determinate and authoritative; derivational background remains secondary because the local work is genitive anchoring. The word also concentrates the surah's divine-authority thread into the phrase that measures faith-refusal and denial.

topics.headline: divine name anchors the verdict source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears whose rejection is being ranked before learning that it exceeds theirs.
topics.reason: The proper noun is genitive inside the construct, making the first maqt definite and sourced in divine evaluation.

topics.headline: proper name governs broader divine-authority links
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the name to faith and denial authority, while derivational disputes stay subordinate to the local proper-name function.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply derivational and co-occurrence background, but the local construct grammar selects the proper divine name as evaluator.

words.gloss_range: elative predicate ranking divine maqt as morally greater than the addressees self-maqt, with the comparison completed by the following standard
words.root_gloss_range: root field of largeness, greatness, seriousness, and moral gravity; the local elative ranks divine rejection over the human baseline
words.prose: {{ar:أَكْبَرُ}} ({{tr:akbaru}}) is the comparison's pivot. As a nominal elative predicate, it ranks divine maqt over the self-maqt baseline without narrating a new event of becoming great. The root's gravity range makes the ranking moral, not merely quantitative, and same-surah arrogance pressure stays contextual as part of what divine judgment weighs. The contrast with divine approval being greater (9:72) sharpens the reversal: here the greater term is rejection.

topics.headline: elative ranks the two maqt phrases
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this word as the hinge that forces divine rejection and self-revulsion onto one scale.
topics.reason: The elative predicate governs a comparative standard and sits between the two maqt phrases.

topics.headline: greatness means moral gravity here
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the comparison as a judgment of gravity, while arrogance-related root pressure remains contextual rather than replacing the elative sense.
topics.reason: The root field supports seriousness and gravity with arrogance pressure in nearby recurrence, but the local form remains the elative predicate.

topics.headline: greater rejection reverses greater approval
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast with divine approval being greater elsewhere (9:72): 40:10 reverses the register so divine rejection is the greater term.
topics.reason: The concrete 9:72 comparison supplies a valid contrast without changing the local syntax.

words.gloss_range: comparative preposition introducing the exceeded baseline after the elative, not an ordinary source or partitive particle here
words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) narrows to comparative function after the elative. It introduces the addressees' self-maqt as the exceeded baseline, not as a source or partitive phrase. Its separate placement makes the pivot visible: their self-revulsion is acknowledged, then subordinated to the divine measure.

topics.headline: preposition marks the exceeded baseline
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human self-maqt is not ignored; it is formally admitted as the baseline that divine maqt exceeds.
topics.reason: The preceding elative selects comparative min and governs the following genitive maqt phrase.

topics.headline: separate particle pivots between maqts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels a visible and audible hinge from divine maqt to self-maqt, rather than two unmeasured clauses.
topics.reason: The particle remains a separate word before the second maqt, creating a clear comparison boundary and sound link.

words.gloss_range: possessed verbal noun of severe self-directed maqt, governed as the comparative baseline and linked to an explicit self-object
words.root_gloss_range: rare root field of severe aversion, abhorrence, and condemning rejection; this occurrence makes that field possessed by the addressees and directed inward
words.prose: {{ar:مَقْتِكُمْ}} ({{tr:maqtikum}}) is the second maqt, now possessed by the addressed group and governed as the comparison's baseline. Its verbal-noun ambiguity is productive: it can name the hatred they perform and the hatred that belongs to them, but the following self-object routes that force inward. This self-maqt remains severe moral disgust, and the passive-detested image sharpens the self as hated object. The same rare root mirrors the divine maqt while the changed possessor shows that their real self-condemnation is still exceeded. The following temporal-causal clause supplies its cause, and same-surah recurrence (40:35) keeps arrogant resistance in the maqt field.

topics.headline: possessed verbal noun turns hatred inward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the addressees as both owners and agents of a hatred that is routed into their own selves.
topics.reason: The suffix supplies the possessor/semantic subject of the verbal noun, and the next word supplies its object.

topics.headline: second maqt mirrors but cannot outrank the first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a controlled contrast: the same maqt root returns with a human possessor as the baseline exceeded by divine judgment.
topics.reason: The genitive under comparative min and repeated root make this occurrence the measured human baseline.

topics.headline: self-maqt remains severe
topics.reader_payoff: The reader does not trivialize their self-loathing; it is severe moral disgust, while derivative passive pressure sharpens the self as hated object.
topics.reason: The same severe maqt field survives here, and derivative evidence is kept as image pressure because the local phrase supplies the actual self-object.

topics.headline: self-maqt waits for its cause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader expects an explanation for self-maqt, which the following temporal-causal clause supplies; same-surah maqt recurrence (40:35) keeps arrogant resistance in view.
topics.reason: The word occurs before the explanatory particle, and the concrete 40:35 recurrence supports a local maqt field.

words.gloss_range: plural possessed self-object of the verbal noun, making the addressees both owners and targets of the inward condemnation
words.root_gloss_range: root field spanning self, person, soul, life, breath, and value; the local plural object selects accountable selves as the target of self-condemnation
words.prose: {{ar:أَنفُسَكُمْ}} ({{tr:anfusakum}}) supplies the object of the possessed verbal noun, making the rebuke reflexive rather than merely emotional. The plural suffix routes the target back to the same addressees and distributes self-condemnation across the group. The self-root range adds living accountable personhood, and its value pressure is inverted: what should be guarded as selfhood becomes what they loathe. The hatred reaches the selves that refused the call, not a detachable mood.

topics.headline: self-object completes inward hatred
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar makes the condemned group both owners and targets of the hatred.
topics.reason: Attachment marks the word as the object complement of the verbal noun, while the suffix maintains referent continuity and compact reflexivity.

topics.headline: self means accountable living personhood
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the object as accountable selves with life and value pressure, while local grammar prevents turning it into an external body-part or abstract pronoun only.
topics.reason: The root range supports self, soul, person, and life; the maqt frame selects accountable selfhood and the 39:53 link provides a concrete harmed-selves parallel.

words.gloss_range: temporal-causal particle that turns the comparison backward to the remembered invitation as the reason for self-maqt
words.prose: {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}) pivots the verdict backward. It attaches the self-maqt phrase to the remembered moment when they were being called to faith, so the particle carries time and cause together. It also nests an earlier invitation inside the later proclamation: judgment is heard as memory replayed against them.

topics.headline: remembered time explains self-maqt
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that self-maqt is explained by a remembered invitation, not left as unexplained remorse.
topics.reason: Attachment routes the temporal clause backward to the comparison/self-maqt frame, and the standalone particle opens the explanatory clause.

topics.headline: earlier call nested inside later call
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the verdict as a replay: the later public call contains the earlier faith-call they refused.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the remembered passive invitation after the passive proclamation, producing a nested call scene.

words.gloss_range: passive imperfect invitation addressed to the condemned group, with the caller uncentered and faith marked as the goal
words.root_gloss_range: root field of calling, inviting, appealing, summoning, and claim-making; the local passive with a goal preposition selects invitation that demands response
words.prose: {{ar:تُدْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:tudʿawna}}) makes the addressees patients of an invitation whose caller is not foregrounded. The passive imperfect keeps that missed opportunity vivid in memory, and the goal phrase makes the invitation responsive rather than a bare announcement. Because the refused invitation becomes the claim against them, the word turns opportunity into evidence. Its root and form contrast with the earlier public proclamation: one call invited them toward faith; the other now exposes what they refused, while the same group is shifted from third-person classification into direct you-address. The call-to-God register is reinforced by the concrete praise of calling to God (41:33).

topics.headline: passive invitation foregrounds recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the condemned group as recipients of a remembered invitation, not as callers or detached observers.
topics.reason: The passive second-plural imperfect suppresses the external caller and foregrounds the addressees and their obligation.

topics.headline: invitation seeks response toward faith
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a responsive invitation toward faith that later becomes evidence against them, with the broader call-to-God field visible (41:33).
topics.reason: The verb is completed by a goal preposition; claim/plea pressure survives as evidentiary color but the local sense is invitation toward faith.

topics.headline: invitation-call differs from proclamation-call
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes the earlier invitation from the later verdict-call while feeling the shift from third-person classification into direct accusation.
topics.reason: The two call roots and passive forms create register contrast; the boundary row keeps the mercy-versus-refusal frame visible.

words.gloss_range: goal preposition after the invitation verb, making faith the destination refused rather than a loose topic
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ilā}}) gives the passive invitation a destination. After the call verb, it selects movement toward faith rather than a loose topic of conversation, and it formally governs the following noun. That positive vector matters because the next particle reverses it into denial, marking the path opposite the prior mercy-success outcome.

topics.headline: preposition makes faith the call goal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that faith is the destination of the call, not merely its subject matter.
topics.reason: The preposition attaches to the passive call verb and governs the following faith noun as its goal.

topics.headline: direction is immediately reversed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels a forward movement toward faith just before the structure turns it into refusal, contrasting the prior mercy-success outcome.
topics.reason: The following close-sequence denial reverses the goal vector, and the boundary row supports the contrast with prior success.

words.gloss_range: definite verbal noun naming faith as the known goal of the invitation: a trust-security state set directly against denial
words.root_gloss_range: root field of faith, trust, security, and entrusted fidelity; the local verbal noun names a definite destination of trust rather than a mere opinion
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْإِيمَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-īmāni}}) is the definite destination of the call. Its article presents faith as a recognized domain, and its verbal-noun form names a state of trust rather than an imperative command. The root's trust-security field makes the refused goal more than assent; it is secure entrusted fidelity. Placed immediately before the denial verb, faith and covering-refusal collide at the ayah's close, and the initial catch at the goal marks the destination before denial. Same-surah recurrence sharpens the refusal thread (40:12).

topics.headline: definite verbal noun is the call goal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees faith as a known destination toward which they were called before it ever became theirs.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the goal preposition, definite by article, and expressed as a verbal noun rather than an imperative.

topics.headline: faith carries trust and security pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the offered destination as a secure trust relation and entrusted fidelity, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as faith/trust rather than free derivative expansion.
topics.reason: The root field supports faith, trust, security, and responsibility; concrete links to 40:12 and 49:14 qualify the refusal without replacing the local noun.

topics.headline: faith stands beside the rejecting act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the invited trust-domain and the denial verb touch syntactically and audibly, compressing the contradiction.
topics.reason: The local adjacency to the closing denial and the root-pair co-occurrence support the trust-versus-covering polarity.

words.gloss_range: close-sequence particle binding the invitation to the contrary denial as immediate response and reversal
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) binds the invitation to the denial as a tight sequel. It is not loose coordination; it fuses timing and moral response so that denial reads as the immediate answer to the call. After the movement toward faith, the particle performs the turn into the final contrary act, anchoring why the prior success frame gives way to the opposite outcome.

topics.headline: close sequence makes denial the response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees denial as the immediate response to invitation, not an unrelated later fact.
topics.reason: The particle is fused to the following imperfect and marks close sequence/consequence rather than loose coordination.

topics.headline: particle reverses the faith vector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the positive movement toward faith pivot into refusal, explaining the transition from prior success language to the contrary outcome.
topics.reason: The prepositional goal before it and denial verb after it make the particle a structural hinge of reversal.

words.gloss_range: second-person Form I imperfect denial closing the ayah as vivid, direct, objectless refusal of the offered faith relation
words.root_gloss_range: root field of covering, refusal, ingratitude, and denial; the closing imperfect selects direct refusal of the faith-call while leaving denial objectless and broad
words.prose: {{ar:تَكْفُرُونَ}} ({{tr:takfurūn}}) closes the ayah on the addressees' own act. The imperfect second-person form revives the refusal inside direct address, and the particle attached to it makes the act grammatically inseparable from the invitation it rejects. In context, the root selects denial of the offered faith relation while remaining objectless enough to cover the call, faith, and divine authority. The final return of the opening denial root leaves responsibility as the last sound, with favor-denial consequence echoed by 14:7.

topics.headline: second-person imperfect revives refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the remembered refusal happening again in direct address, tightly attached to the invitation sequence.
topics.reason: The second-plural imperfect carries the subject, reports rather than commands, and is linked by the fused sequence particle.

topics.headline: objectless denial spreads over the offered relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the denial as refusal of the faith-call, while its lack of direct object lets the refusal cover the offered faith, the call, and authority behind it.
topics.reason: The faith-call context selects denial over generic ingratitude, and the absence of a direct object broadens local scope without importing derived-form force.

topics.headline: denial after favor echoes severe consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects denial after invitation here with denial after favor and severe consequence (14:7).
topics.reason: The concrete 14:7 reference supports a consequence-field echo while the local wording remains the controlling parse.

topics.headline: closing denial answers opening denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends on human responsibility: the root that classified them returns as the final direct accusation around the rejected faith center.
topics.reason: The root occurs near the opening and at the final word, framing faith as the rejected center and leaving the human act last.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: لَمَقْتُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ مِن مَّقْتِكُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ
baseline_models.mechanism: The repeated maqt sets two severe aversions toward the same ugly refusal on one comparative scale: divine appraisal exceeds the offenders' later reflexive appraisal.

activation_trace.role: Severe abhorrence of ugly conduct supplies both terms of the comparison rather than two unrelated emotions.
Magnitude opposed to smallness makes akbar a calibration of unequal moral measures.
The self as the thing's own identity makes the second maqt reflexive and turns judgment inward.

changed_reading.before: A future announcement says that God hated them more than they hated themselves.
changed_reading.after: The announcement compares an already exact divine valuation of their ugly refusal with their belated, still smaller act of self-valuation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: يُنَادَوْنَ ... إِذْ تُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلْإِيمَٰنِ فَتَكْفُرُونَ
baseline_models.mechanism: Two passive calls form a temporal reversal: an earlier invitation that allowed response is answered by covering, then a later public summons announces the consequence and allows no evasive response.

activation_trace.role: Raised voice and calling make the later address an audible summons.
The parallel mapped inventory reinforces the public, extended voice of the summons.
Calling that inclines another by speech gives the earlier invitation a directional offer.
Heart-settling assent names the offered destination of the earlier call.
Blocking the truth is both the identity announced at the start and the immediate response marked by the final fa.

changed_reading.before: The verse contains an announcement and a recollection of an invitation.
changed_reading.after: The announcement is the returned form of the rejected invitation: the voice they would not answer becomes the voice that publicly fixes what their answer was.

baseline_models.mechanism: The same root opens and closes the ayah, enclosing the summons, comparison, self, and invitation inside a repeated act of covering; the final fa presents covering as a produced response, not merely a static label.

activation_trace.role: Literal covering supplies the enclosing material image around everything said between the two occurrences.
Obstruction of truth specifies what the repeated covering does at the invitation.
The spoken inclination toward faith is the incoming movement that the covering blocks.

changed_reading.before: Kafaru simply classifies the addressees, and takfurun repeats that classification.
changed_reading.after: The first occurrence names the settled enclosure whose formation the last clause replays: a call arrives, and they actively cover its destination.

context_deltas.mechanism: The prelude contrasts two coverings: human covering blocks truth, while divine covering shields a returned sinner from a sin's effect. Mercy's breadth makes the contrast functional rather than merely verbal.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the shared material operation whose object and result differ.
Covering a sin while protecting its bearer supplies the reparative counterpart to obstructive covering.
Repeated requests for protected covering keep that reparative possibility immediately before the focus.
Expansiveness opposed to constriction prevents the focus maqt from being read as the only available divine relation.
Tender mercy names the wider field within which protective covering is requested.

structural_cues: 40:3 names forgiveness, accepted return, and severe consequence together.
40:7-9 immediately precede the focus with intercession, expansive mercy, forgiveness, protection, and rescue.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent obstructive and protective branch images of covering; I infer a contrast based on what is covered and toward what end. The live alternative is simple lexical recurrence without deliberate material counterpoint.

changed_reading.before: Their kufr is only a covered refusal that incurs divine aversion.
changed_reading.after: Their obstructive covering rejects the very relation in which another kind of covering could protect them; the maqt marks refusal of an already-open reparative possibility.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate reply and diagnosis convert generic unbelief into asymmetric allegiance: they confess only after the summons, and in life they rejected when God alone was invoked but assented when partnership was introduced.

activation_trace.role: Admission and submission turn the focus self-maqt into belated acknowledgment rather than mere distress.
Named sins give the belated inward aversion a confessed object.
Calling by speech repeats the focus invitation and specifies its disputed object.
Divine oneness without partner supplies the condition under which they refused.
Blocking truth is explicitly paired with the call to God alone.
Association with God supplies the rival condition under which assent became acceptable.
Assent appears on the partnership side of the conditional mirror, exposing selective rather than absent belief.

structural_cues: 40:11 is the speakers' direct response to the proclamation in 40:10.
40:12 begins with a causal diagnosis and mirrors call-alone/reject against partnership/assent.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies confession followed by an explicit conditional asymmetry; I infer that 40:12 diagnoses the refusal recalled in 40:10. A live alternative is that 40:12 explains the punishment generally rather than every nuance of the focus invitation.

changed_reading.before: They were called to faith but lacked or rejected belief.
changed_reading.after: They were capable of assent but refused its exclusive direction; their later self-maqt recognizes a chosen allegiance pattern exposed by the summons.

context_deltas.mechanism: Judgment removes the cover spatially and epistemically: persons stand exposed, each self receives what it acquired, and even what chests hide is known. Self-maqt is therefore forced self-recognition under complete disclosure.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the condition that the later exposure reverses.
The self as one's own identity anchors the disclosed account back to anfusakum.
Appearance and uncovering turn judgment into an exposed field.
Concealment is explicitly negated, closing the hiding function of kufr.
Act-for-act requital supplies the accounting mechanism behind the comparative aversion.
Every individual identity is made the unit that receives its own account.
Acquisition makes the disclosed outcome something accumulated by the self.
The chest as the source from which acts issue locates the previously hidden interior now known.

structural_cues: 40:16 repeats the judgment day and negates all hiding.
40:17 places every nafs in an exact acquisition-to-requital relation.
40:19 moves disclosure from public appearance to concealed interior sources.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies covering, exposure, individual requital, acquisition, and known interiors; I infer that disclosure causes the self-directed maqt. The alternative is that self-maqt is simply another punishment emotion alongside, not produced by, accounting.

changed_reading.before: They happen to hate themselves when punishment arrives.
changed_reading.after: Their self-hatred is the subjective recoil of an uncovered account: the covering fails, the acquired act is returned to its own self, and no hidden interior can soften it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later maqt recurrence identifies a self-reinforcing mechanism: unsupported argument twists around signs, pride occupies the inner source, and repeated refusal takes a seal-like form. The same akbar-min frame elsewhere confirms scalar calibration.

activation_trace.role: The focus's doubled severe abhorrence is the relation that the later recurrence diagnoses.
The inward field of reasoning and intent allows heart and chest cues to specify what the hated self had been doing.
Twisted contention supplies the active conduct that attracts the repeated maqt.
The absent compelling warrant makes the contention self-authorized rather than evidence-driven.
The exact severe-aversion branch recurs around unsupported disputation.
Stamping and sealing turn reiterated refusal into a fixed receptive surface.
The heart locates the sealed surface in the inner organ of orientation.
Grandeur and self-exaltation connect the greatness of the aversion with the disputant's arrogated greatness.
The chest as the source of action houses the pride driving the dispute.
A second akbar-min construction confirms that the surah uses this form to correct mismatched scales.

structural_cues: 40:35 repeats both maqt and k-b-r, then links the pattern to a sealed arrogant heart.
40:56 repeats unsupported disputation and locates unattainable pride in the chests.
40:57 repeats the exact comparative frame akbar min for cosmic scale.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact lexical and constructional recurrences plus inner sealing; I infer that they explain why the focus comparison is unequal. The alternative is that these are parallel examples of arrogance and scale, not a direct causal gloss on 40:10.

changed_reading.before: God's maqt is greater as an unexplained difference of emotional intensity.
changed_reading.after: The greater measure answers a self-sealing distortion of scale: unsupported contention magnifies the self, blocks reception, and can appraise itself accurately only after the seal's world collapses.

context_deltas.mechanism: The believer's speech stages reciprocal calls with opposed destinations: rescue versus fire, kufr and partnership versus the Mighty Forgiver. The focus invitation is one vector in a contested social field, and the judgment summons reveals which vector actually returned everyone to God.

activation_trace.role: A spoken inclination toward a destination anchors the focus invitation as directional.
Two reciprocal calls expose opposed attempts to incline one another.
Rescue by separation supplies the destination of the believer's call.
The reciprocal call is restated with its theological destinations made explicit.
Blocking truth is named as the destination toward which the opposing group calls.
Partnership specifies the rival allegiance carried by that call.
The protecting Forgiver marks the reparative destination of the counter-call.
Return to a destination closes the directional contest at God.

structural_cues: 40:41 balances I call you against you call me with rescue and fire as explicit endpoints.
40:42 specifies the opposed calls as kufr/partnership and the Mighty/Forgiver.
40:43 denies effective call to the rival object and states the common return to God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies grammatically reciprocal calls and opposed destinations; I infer that this social contest instantiates the focus's call to faith. The alternative is that the narrative is an analogous later episode rather than the specific invitation remembered in 40:10.

changed_reading.before: The call to faith is a single message delivered to isolated hearers.
changed_reading.after: The call enters a reciprocal struggle of inclinations; refusing it means answering a counter-call toward partnership, and the final summons exposes the destination chosen.

context_deltas.mechanism: Those who would not answer messengers later ask the keepers to call for relief, but their call is declared lost. The call-response promise and the contrast between arrogance and abasement make nonresponse a refused relation that returns as an unanswered request.

activation_trace.role: The original spoken invitation supplies the unanswered first side of the relation.
The condemned now delegate a call for relief, reversing their earlier position as recipients.
Messengers and message identify the prior channel whose arrival they concede.
Meaning made clear by signs removes lack of disclosure as the reason for nonresponse.
The repeated call is now issued without an effective destination or answer.
Missing the intended direction characterizes the late call's failure.
The direct invitation to call supplies the open relational offer.
Answering speech supplies the promised responsive return.
Self-exaltation identifies what blocks entry into the call-response relation.
Abasement supplies the reversed posture reached after arrogant nonresponse.

structural_cues: 40:49-50 reverses call roles: former recipients become petitioners and concede that messengers came clearly.
40:60 places call and answer in one clause, then contrasts arrogant refusal with humbled entry.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a prior clear message, a later futile call, an explicit call-answer pair, and arrogance followed by abasement; I infer a returned relational failure. The alternative is that prayer and proclamation are distinct call types joined only thematically.

changed_reading.before: Their fault is rejection of the content called faith.
changed_reading.after: Their fault also has a response structure: they reject an open call-answer relation, then discover that their own urgent call no longer reaches an answer.

context_deltas.mechanism: At visible force the earlier polarity reverses exactly: they affirm God alone and disavow what they had associated, yet this faith no longer benefits. The decisive variable is not bare possession of belief-language but its target and timing before coercive sight.

activation_trace.role: Heart-settling assent is the response offered before visible compulsion.
The focus occurrence blocks truth when the invitation still permits a consequential response.
Direct sight supplies the coercive evidentiary threshold at which the reversal occurs.
Overwhelming force is what has become visible and now drives assent.
The same assent branch appears after sight, preserving content while changing timing.
Oneness without partner is now affirmed, reversing the asymmetry diagnosed in 40:12.
Disavowal and disengagement let the same root now target the former partners rather than truth.
Association names what their belated kufr finally repudiates.
The negation of benefit marks the closed response window despite corrected content.
Belated assent remains lexically faith while being pragmatically ineffective.

structural_cues: 40:84 reverses 40:12's pairing: God alone now receives faith and the associated objects receive kufr.
40:85 states that faith after seeing force does not benefit.
The focus's idh and final fa preserve the earlier response moment as the morally diagnostic one.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an exact polarity reversal and explicitly negated benefit; I infer that timing and target, not the mere words iman and kufr, govern the focus comparison. The alternative is that the closing scene supplies a general historical rule rather than directly resolving 40:10's temporal force.

changed_reading.before: Faith and kufr are fixed labels for two kinds of people.
changed_reading.after: They are directed responses whose objects can reverse: the condemned eventually utter the right assent and deploy kufr as repudiation of partnership, but only after sight has removed the freedom that made the earlier call answerable.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's form-distant n-w-d target for n-d-w. It remains anchored in yunadawna and gains directional support from the surah's explicit overturning and turning-away cues, but downstream prose should present it only as a kinetic branch-image, not as the lexical meaning of the verb.

activation_trace.role: Swaying and movement add a contained kinetic image to the otherwise audible summons.
The named day of mutual calling extends that kinetic image from one summons to the judgment scene.
Overturning something from its direction supplies the long prior motion that judgment arrests.
Being turned from a face or direction reinforces recurrent directional displacement.

changed_reading.before: They are audibly summoned to hear a verdict.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the summons also arrests a history of swerving: those repeatedly turned from the call are finally made to face one public direction.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because anfusakum ordinarily denotes the persons themselves, while the activated branch foregrounds force, grandeur, and pride. It remains anchored in the packet's n-f-s inventory and is sharpened by pride located in hearts and chests, but prose should say the self is read as a pride-bearing self-formation, not claim that nafs simply means arrogance here.

activation_trace.role: Force of self, grandeur, and pride make the object of hatred a previously inflated self-formation.
Self-exaltation joins great maqt to the arrogant subject who generated it.
The heart locates that self-exalting formation inwardly.
The chest as an originating interior houses the stated pride.
Unattainable self-exaltation supplies the structure that later collapses into self-maqt.

changed_reading.before: They hate their bare selves because those selves are suffering.
changed_reading.after: They hate the magnified self they had built and obeyed: judgment collapses its claimed greatness, leaving that self-construction as the immediate object of recoil.

strongest_changes: The immediate sequel makes the rejected faith-call a selective allegiance problem: they could assent to partnership but not to God alone.
Exposure and individual requital turn self-maqt into the recoil of an uncovered account rather than an unstructured punishment emotion.
Reciprocal calls and the later failed petition make the focus a reversed call-response relation.
The closing polarity reversal shows that correct faith and disavowal after coercive sight are too late, sharpening the temporal force of idh.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah recurrence did not merely amplify punishment. It differentiated kinds of covering, traced calls toward opposed destinations, repeated maqt with sealed inner pride, and finally let the same kufr root change target when the response window had closed.
remaining_uncertainties: The protective-covering contrast between gh-f-r and k-f-r is materially coherent but may be associative rather than an intended lexical pairing.
The social call scenes clearly instantiate the mechanism, but they need not be the identical historical invitation recalled by the focus.
The n-w-d swaying image is explicitly form-distant and should remain exploratory.
The pride-bearing nafs reading supplements rather than replaces the ordinary reflexive sense of anfusakum.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The call reopens a refused attraction.** `د ع و/B001` is calling that draws near by speech; it appears retrospectively inside the announcement of `م ق ت/B001`, severe loathing for blameworthy ugliness. I infer that the former invitation now functions as evidence: refusal of the drawing call generated the ugliness being condemned. The ayah reads self-loathing as belated recognition of resisted approach.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The call-and-response opening in 40:60 reveals that the earlier refused call was a genuine relational channel; self-loathing follows refusal of reciprocity.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The two loathings are two times of recognition.** Lexically, `م ق ت:B001` is "severe loathing for ugliness," while `ن ف س:B013` is inner mind or hidden intent. Structurally, the ayah compares God's prior loathing at the refused call with the addressees' present self-loathing; 40:11 then turns that inner recoil into confession. Self-loathing plays the role of delayed inward recognition of an ugliness already judged. The packet supplies the comparative and temporal `إذ`; I infer that refusal produced the ugliness now seen from within. The call therefore exposes a judgment lag: the divine evaluation precedes and exceeds the self's eventual verdict on itself.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 40:83-85 completes the recognition lag: self-satisfied knowledge yields only when force is seen, and the resulting assent arrives too late to benefit.

baseline.text: İnkâr edenlere şöyle seslenilir: Siz imana çağrıldığınızda inkâr ediyordunuz; Allah'ın size öfkesi, kendinize duyduğunuz öfkeden daha büyüktür.

findings.text: Daha önce reddedilen iman çağrısı şimdi delile dönüşür: kişinin kendine öfkesi, yaklaşma çağrısına direnirken oluşan çirkinliği geç fark etmesidir.
Allah'ın değerlendirmesi ile kişinin kendisi hakkındaki hükmü arasında zaman farkı vardır; içteki geç tanıma, daha önce verilmiş hükme ancak sonuç aşamasında yetişir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi örtme ve görünmez kılma çekirdeğini; zırhı giysiyle kaplama, silahla örtünme, külün toprakla kapanması ve yıldızların güneş ışığında görünmemesi gibi gerçekleşmelerle açıkça destekler.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başka bir şeyle örterek görünmesini engellemek veya kapalı duruma getirmektir. Zırhın giysiyle, kişinin silahla ya da külün savrulan toprakla örtülmesi bu işlemin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin üstünü kapatarak onu görünmez veya örtülü duruma getirme işlemi.
Zırhı giysiyle kaplama, silahla örtünme ve külün üstünün toprakla kapanması çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.
Güneşin yıldızları görünmez kılması da görsel örtme sonucu üzerinden bu çekirdeğe bağlanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar örtme ve kapatma çekirdeğinde birleşir; farklı örnekler bu işlemin nesne, giysi, silah, kül ve gök görünümü üzerindeki gerçekleşmelerini gösterir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi karanlık geceyi, denizi, büyük ırmağı, gün batımını ve bulutu aynı adlandırma çevresinde toplar; bunların tümünü tek bir gerçek 'kuşatan örtü' türü saymak yerine, karanlık, genişlik veya kapatma etkisiyle örten farklı varlıklar olarak anlamak gerekir.
